goal: First-person lived experience, not presumed choices or horoscope claims
participant_header: Optional Life Patterns research pilot. Not the live survey; no chart predictions or clinical assessment. You may decline any question or stop. Answers stay in this browser tab until you export a file; nothing is uploaded or automatically stored.
scope: Independent opt-in pilot only. Do not append to historical or existing active interviews or alter frozen model predictions.
response_rules: Every dimension starts NOT_ASKED; an unselected topic is never coded as absent or zero.
NEVER, UNKNOWN, SKIPPED, ANSWERED, ALREADY_COVERED and NOT_ASKED are distinct states.
Answering a broad adjacent domain is not equivalent evidence; require a supported prior-source phrase covering the actual measured experience and recall window.
If a question is already adequately answered, mark ALREADY_COVERED with a source reference instead of restating it.
Ask one short question at a time; any follow-up is optional and must resolve a specific unanswered distinction, not finish a quota.
Participant can report context variation or different earlier-life periods. Never force a typical answer or numeric precision.
Interpretations of higher guidance/coincidence remain subjective reports, not proof of external cause.
Keep personal meaning separate from perceived social impact; sudden insight separate from action; surprise separate from awe.
Do not derive a trait score, diagnosis or natal prediction from this module.
predictability_options: Changes greatly by period or area

items.purpose: How unexpected your own reactions feel, separately from what other people do.
items.question: Over the past year, how often have your own thoughts, feelings, or actions genuinely surprised you?
items.optional_followup: Was anything particularly surprising about how you reacted, or do different parts of life differ?
items.optional_intensity: If this has happened, how strongly did you feel surprised at its peak?

items.purpose: Surprise about people and the world, which need not match surprise about yourself.
items.question: Over the past year, how often have other people or things happening in the world genuinely surprised or shocked you?
items.optional_followup: If they differ, which happens more: surprises about other people, or about the wider world? Were the surprises mostly pleasant, upsetting or mixed?
items.optional_intensity: If this has happened, how strongly did you feel surprised at its peak?

items.purpose: How often and intensely you feel awe or wonder; this is different from novelty or positive mood.
items.question: In the past year, how often, if at all, have you felt awe or wonder?
items.optional_followup: What tends to evoke it for you, if anything—perhaps people, nature, art, ideas, everyday life, or something else?
items.optional_intensity: If this has happened, how powerful did the feeling get?

items.purpose: Sudden changes in understanding, without assuming they led to changed behavior.
items.question: Over the past year, how often have you suddenly realized something important about yourself, another person, or life that you did not see before?
items.optional_followup: Did any such realization change what you did, or did it mainly change how you saw things? Gradual changes count separately.
items.optional_intensity: If this has happened, how important did the largest realization feel?

items.purpose: Everyday stability or disruption, separate from sudden changes in perspective.
items.question: Over the past year, how predictable or unpredictable has your day-to-day life felt?
items.optional_followup: If they differ, was that because of external events, changes in how you understood things, or both? Has this changed during different parts of your life?

items.purpose: The felt sense of being guided, without assuming a religious belief or supernatural cause.
items.question: In the past year, how often, if ever, has it felt as though something beyond your deliberate plans was guiding events in your life?
items.optional_followup: What interpretation, if any, do you give that feeling? 'I don't believe that happens' is a complete answer.
items.optional_intensity: If this has happened, how strong was the feeling at its peak?

items.purpose: Noticing meaningful coincidences, separately from what you believe caused them.
items.question: Over the past year, how often, if ever, have coincidences struck you as unusually meaningful?
items.optional_followup: When you reconsider them later, do they still seem meaningful, seem like chance, or does it vary?
items.optional_intensity: If this has happened, how powerful was the feeling of significance?

items.purpose: How meaningful life feels to you and separately how much difference you feel you make to others.
items.question: Right now, how meaningful does your life feel to you personally? Separately, how much difference do you feel you make to other people or the world?

prompt_fields.label: Life feels meaningful to me personally
I feel I make a difference to others or the world

items.optional_followup: Is that a settled feeling, something you are still looking for, or something that changes over time?

topic_selection.description: After core questions, offer all four other topics by neutral names. Selection reflects interest, never the measured frequency; do not infer absent experience for unselected topics.

labels.EM02: Surprises about people and the world
labels.EM06: A sense of guidance beyond your plans

source_refinement_note: New neutral measurement phrasing informed by the owner's experience categories, not mapped by assumption to classical astrological chart rules.
validation_plan: Check whether respondents can answer without leading assumptions or examples.
Check whether people distinguish self surprise, awe, abrupt insight, and life meaning.
Check item nonredundancy against prior interview source in blinded review.
Run repeat-response reliability/discriminant pilot before any prospectively frozen chart study.
